title: rag-eval-kit
summary: A Python package for comparing RAG pipelines on answer quality, retrieval, latency, and cost.
contribution: I built the evaluation runner, adapters, metrics, and reporting.
details: Connect a pipeline, supply labeled questions, and choose metrics or a parameter sweep. The runner saves individual answers and produces CSV exports and HTML comparison reports. It supports common RAG frameworks, parallel queries, and resumable runs.
usage: Install rag-eval-kit from PyPI and follow the repository’s configuration examples.

title: NeuroTechML
eyebrow: From recorded signals to streaming inference
summary: Student-team research on recognizing speech sounds from facial and neck muscle signals.
contribution: As NeuroTechSC’s ML and Data Team Lead, I worked on preprocessing, training, analysis, and live integration.
details: We processed surface EMG recordings, trained LSTM classifiers, and tried live inference. The work covered 44 phonemes plus a rest class, but isolated-sound training did not transfer reliably to continuous speech or subvocalization.
usage: The repository contains notebooks, saved models, and findings.

title: Custom LLM Harness
eyebrow: Model access, agent execution, and evaluation
summary: A custom harness for serving language models, running agents, and inspecting their results.
contribution: I built the harness and evaluation workflow around upstream models, OpenCode, vLLM, Harbor, and Terminal-Bench.
details: It manages inference endpoints, tool execution, evaluation runs, and transcripts. I use it to compare agent configurations and distinguish task failures from infrastructure problems.
A 180-trial comparison on 30 Terminal-Bench tasks did not establish an improvement from an optional delegation workflow. Neither configuration actually invoked the secondary workers.
note: Source and hosted access are private. A study summary is available below.

title: llm-scry
eyebrow: An unfinished interface to transformer internals
summary: A local API prototype for inspecting generated tokens, attention patterns, and model activations.
contribution: I built the API, activation capture, and session handling.
details: Built around TransformerLens, it streams token probabilities and exposes attention by layer and head. It was an early experiment in making model internals easier to inspect.
note: The frontend is incomplete. There is no hosted demo, and activation patching is not implemented.

title: TransferBatch
eyebrow: Production sheets with an accountable order trail
summary: A Shopify-connected tool that arranges transfer-print orders onto production sheets.
contribution: I built the layout engine, order integration, checks, and deployment.
imageCaption: Actual application running with demonstration data.
imageAlt: TransferBatch batch review with verified production sheet layout and sample artwork
details: Map artwork to order items, set dimensions, then prepare and verify a sheet before issuing it. Checks preserve copy counts and artwork size, while a manifest tracks each transfer back to its order.
usage: Visit TransferBatch to see the product. The deployed workflow has been tested with a Shopify development-store order; commercial launch is still in preparation.

title: SheetMason
eyebrow: Document automation that preserves the original
summary: A desktop tool for naming drawing sheets and splitting large PDF sets.
contribution: I built the PDF pipeline, review interface, and local OCR integration.
imageCaption: Actual application running with demonstration data.
imageAlt: SheetMason desktop review with a synthetic drawing, sheet labels, and source crops
details: Select the title-block region, review extracted sheet labels, and export individually named PDFs. Original files stay unchanged, and each output remains traceable to its source page.
note: Local alpha; no public download yet. OCR accuracy and operator time savings are not established.

title: Siting Radar
summary: A tool for tracking changes to local energy siting rules in municipal documents.
contribution: I built the collection pipeline, event detection, evidence review, and alert infrastructure.
imageCaption: Actual application running with demonstration data.
imageAlt: Siting Radar alert dashboard using clearly labeled synthetic demonstration signals
details: It searches agendas, minutes, and hearing notices for relevant decisions, with source quotations and page citations. The goal is to make scattered local planning information easier to follow.
usage: Visit the site for coverage and methodology. Historical backtests do not establish live alert accuracy.

title: Living Scenarios
summary: A Jira app that displays Gherkin scenarios alongside their latest CI test results.
contribution: I built the Forge app, CLI, and result mapping.
details: Feature files remain in Git. A CLI uploads the scenarios and test reports from CI, making results visible on Jira work items without giving the app repository credentials.
note: Tested on development and staging sites; marketplace distribution is pending.

title: Answerwell
summary: A Confluence Q&A app with accepted answers, tags, follows, and expert routing.
contribution: I built the app, permission-aware workflows, importers, and notifications.
details: Questions and answers use native Confluence pages and comments. The app adds Q&A organization while respecting the reader’s existing content permissions.
note: Tested on development and staging sites; not yet available on the marketplace.

title: Multithreaded HTTP Server
summary: A multithreaded HTTP server written in C.
contribution: I implemented request handling and synchronization on top of supplied course helpers.
details: Handles GET and PUT requests through a worker queue, with file locking and request-order logging. An earlier course project in concurrency and systems programming.
note: Archived, private source. The original helper library is missing, so it is not a standalone runnable release.

title: Sixdegrees
summary: A C++ program that finds the shortest movie connection between two actors.
contribution: I built the graph, search, input parsing, and path output.
details: Actors and shared films form a graph. A search returns the actor-and-movie chain connecting a requested pair—an earlier project in graph algorithms and data structures.

title: Virtual Viper
summary: A Snake-inspired game made with GDevelop.
contribution: I contributed the initial playable slice, mechanics, graphics, sprites, and audio integration.
details: An earlier team game project, with the shared source available on GitHub.
note: No current hosted build is linked.
